newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent jumps 59 cts on gasoline, technicals.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent jumps 59 cts on gasoline, technicals.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures raced higher on Tuesday to close up 59 cents, backed by a rally in U.S. gasoline markets and underpinned by technical support, brokers said.
August IPE Brent last traded at $18.41 a barrel, off seven cents from the day's high. The contract crept into backwardation against September, which last traded at $18.38, up 52 cents.
"We've retraced the whole of Monday's losses," one commented.
"We began today at the bottom of last week's (trading) range and now we're back at the top of it."
Brent gained sharp impetus from August WTI's break above $19.35 and then $19.50 a barrel. The gains triggered a series of stops amid a flurry of Brent/WTI spread business.
"After $19.50 it was stops all the way," an IPE trader said.

More support came from news that Occidental Petroleum Corp had declared force majeure in its 180,000 barrel per day (bpd) Cano Limon oilfield in eastern Colombia after rebel attacks on a major pipeline.

August WTI was trading 66 cents higher at $19.65. It was also boosted by gasoline, which jumped on talk that Tuesday's report from the American Petroleum Institute (API) will show possibly the last sizeable drawdown of unleaded stocks of the summer.
August NYMEX unleaded was 1.58 cent a gallon higher at 59.93 cents.
August IPE gas oil futures closed $2 a tonne higher at $162.75 after touching $164 in the final hour of business. September settled at $164.25, up $1.75.
